The Fund may use leverage to enhance returns, fund liquidity and bridge investments.

results.name: OrbiMed Genesis Fund
results.management_company_description: As one of the largest healthcare-dedicated investment firms globally, OrbiMed boasts a strong investment platform with $20.2 billion in assets under management and a team of 151 professionals with deep expertise in science, medicine, and finance.  By virtue of OrbiMed’s sizable venture capital activities, the Firm can access a range of distinctive later-stage private investments, PIPE (private investment in public entity) opportunities, and other special situations.
results.strategy_description:
The Genesis Fund takes advantage of OrbiMed's powerful platform to invest in an overlooked market niche: later-stage private opportunities that may be unsuitable for typical venture capital funds as well as less-liquid public equities and special situations that may be passed over by many public market participants.  The fund invests in emerging life sciences companies through "crossover" positions in private companies, initial public offerings, "cornerstone" investments, PIPE transactions, and opportunities in catalyst-driven smaller cap public companies. Investments focus on life sciences companies engaged in the discovery and development of novel products and services that OrbiMed believes will address significant unmet medical needs. 

Genesis Fund investments are subject to a thorough due diligence process and validation by proprietary internal research.  Sources for idea generation include scientific data from industry publications, medical conferences, industry contacts, and rigorous financial reviews of companies across healthcare subsectors. OrbiMed prefers to invest in companies with specific catalysts that could trigger value realization, such as attaining a clinical development or regulatory milestone for a potential blockbuster new drug.

For short positions the Fund targets companies which are over valued, exhibit financial weakness or other risks, poor business models, weak compeitive position and poor industry structures.

The Fund is managed by Jinzhi Jiang (George), Founder and CIO of Greenwoods.

results.management_company_description:
Forada was founded in London, UK, in 2017 by Jon Ridgway. 
The firm is managing over US$ 2bn across the Forada Fund and pari-passu managed accounts.
results.strategy_description:
Forada is a catalyst-driven discretionary macro manager based in London, set up by CIO, Jon Ridgway in 2017. It seeks uncorrelated returns, with low drawdowns and convex upside. Forada focuses on highly liquid macro instruments with emphasis on developed market interest rates, particularly in Europe, US, Japan and the UK. It also adds portfolio diversification using equity indices, foreign exchange and commodities.

Founded in 2017, Forada runs a portfolio via the commingled Forada Master Fund and managed accounts.
Forada's commingled fund launched in May 2021. 
Forada launched an Enhanced  2X levered share class of the existing strategy in January 2026.

Appendix: Enhanced Strategy Backtest Methodology   
Calculations for Enhanced Strategy
Monthly gross returns originate from the i) historical trading returns of the Ixworth SMA (November 2016 - May 2017), Forada SMA (October 2017 – April 2021) and Forada Fund (May 2021 – August 2025) and ii) money market returns (May 2021 – December 2025).
i) Trading returns: the Enhanced share class doubles the risk of existing strategy. For example, if an existing position is 1,000 bund futures, to double the risk the corresponding position is 2,000 bund futures. The historical monthly trading returns or losses are therefore double those of the existing share classes.  
ii) Money market returns: Forada Master Fund holds unencumbered cash in money market funds. The Enhanced share class consumes twice as much encumbered cash, which reduces cash available to earn a money market return. The historical monthly money market returns have been reduced to account for the imputed additional cash usage of the Enhanced share class. Prior to May 2021’s launch of the commingled fund the strategy ran SMAs which did not receive any money market return that a commingled fund may have earned, so no money market return adjustment has been made during that period.  
The doubled trading returns and adjusted money market returns are combined to form the gross returns. 
Fund expenses, 1% management fee and 25% performance fee are applied to calculate the historical net track record.

results.management_company_description:
Kirkoswald is a multinational investment management group, operating across a wide range of asset classes and geographies. Our expertise includes Global Macro, Emerging Local Markets and External Debt, and Private Credit, including both asset-backed and direct lending capabilities. Decades of investment experience and a disciplined risk management approach make Kirkoswald a partner of choice to capital allocators globally.
Kirkoswald combines decades of professional experience in macro and emerging markets investing with institutional knowledge, a rigorous research and risk management process, and experience weathering economic headwinds and market cycles. The firm deploys a range of strategies across various investment products, primarily focused on emerging markets.
Kirkoswald is committed to excellence first and foremost and builds connections with investors to help them diversify their strategy and grow their assets.



Abbeville Partners LLP was formed in 2013 and changed its name to Kirkoswald Capital Partners LLP on 30 January 2018.
results.strategy_description:
Kirkoswald Capital Partners LLP launched a discretionary global macro fund with an emerging market bias, namely the Kirkoswald Global Macro UCITS Fund (“Fund”), on the Investcorp-Tages UCITS platform in January 2022. The investment objective of the Fund is to seek positive returns for investors by investing in global emerging and developed markets. The Fund seeks to achieve the investment objective by executing a discretionary global macro strategy investing across various asset classes, with a primary focus on fixed income securities, currencies and foreign exchange, and to a lesser extent equities.

The investment strategy relies on the analysis of top-down macroeconomic economic drivers and bottom-up technical factors to identify investment opportunities that we believe will generate a return for the Fund by taking long and short exposure to the asset classes. Top-down macro-economic views are formed by assessing a wide range of inputs including fundamental data (e.g., economic statistics, central bank actions), market trading flows and technicals (e.g., price and volume movement), monitoring political events (e.g., referenda and elections) and reviewing research and strategy reports produced by external economists. Bottom-up technical factors may include relative pricing of the securities and the asset flows between various interest rate market participants.

results.management_company_description:
Founded in 1971 and based in Los Angeles, TCW manages a broad range of innovative, actively managed investment products that strive to enhance and protect clients’ wealth. TCW’s clients include many of the largest corporate and public pension plans, financial institutions, insurance companies, endowments and foundations in the United States, as well as a substantial number of international entities including central banks, sovereign wealth funds and private banks.

In 2001, TCW was acquired by Société Générale (SG), one of the largest global banking franchises with a presence in 85 countries. SG worked with TCW to grow and expand its global footprint for a dozen years. The partnership was very productive, including in early 2010, TCW’s acquisition of Metropolitan West Asset Management, LLC (MetWest), a top-ranked fixed income asset manager. As a result, key employees of MetWest assumed primary responsibility for the oversight of TCW’s fixed income mandates. Since that time, MetWest has operated as a subsidiary of The TCW Group, Inc. 

In February 2013, TCW’s management effected a management led buy-out of SG in partnership with The Carlyle Group. Following the buyout, The Carlyle Group held an approximately 60% stake in the firm, with TCW management and employees owning the balance of approximately 40%, on a fully diluted basis. TCW management negotiated strong governance provisions to ensure that TCW’s managerial autonomy would be preserved. Equity for the transaction came from TCW management and two Carlyle investment funds – Carlyle Global Financial Services Partners, a $1.1 billion financial services fund, and Carlyle Partners V, a $13.7 billion U.S. buyout fund. The Carlyle transaction facilitated a management initiative to increase employee ownership.  Prior to 2010, TCW employees did not have significant equity interests in the firm. Since the 2010 acquisition of MetWest by TCW, employee ownership has continued to increase.

On December 27, 2017, Nippon Life completed its acquisition of a 24.75% minority stake in TCW from Carlyle. As a result of this transaction, ownership in TCW by TCW management and employees increased to 44.07%, and Carlyle maintains a 31.18% interest in the firm through a purchase by its long duration private equity fund, Carlyle Global Partners.

There is a high level of employee ownership of the company, including most of TCW’s key decision-making investment and other professionals. TCW believes strongly that employee equity ownership aligns the interests of the decision-making employees with the interests of the firm and the firm’s clients, and creates a cohesive “ownership culture.”

Nippon and Carlyle have agreed to continue the existing strong governance protections for TCW management, which help to ensure that TCW’s current management and investment teams are primarily responsible for personnel and compensation decisions, and solely responsible for the management of investment portfolios.

results.management_company_description: Tidan Capital is a Stockholm-based, independent investment management company established in 2020 by Brummer & Partners alumni with several decades of investment experience across the capital structure. Our flagship strategy, a market-neutral credit relative value approach, is built on a foundation of deep fundamental analysis and a disciplined investment process. With a presence in Europe and expanding globally, Tidan Capital operates under rigorous regulatory standards and an organisation relying on premier service providers ensuring a scalable and governance-focused investment platform for our clients.
results.strategy_description:
Themis is Tidan Capital’s dedicated equity market neutral strategy, built on a carve-out from the flagship Tidan program. The strategy seeks to generate consistent alpha by exploiting value creation and dilution across single stocks—through long and short positions—with limited reliance on index or factor hedging. Themis applies a deep fundamental approach, underpinned by credit analysis, to identify companies undergoing structural or financial transitions that are not yet fully reflected in equity valuations.

The investment process focuses on isolating idiosyncratic opportunities, particularly in companies where credit dynamics signal upcoming equity repricing. Typical candidates include those facing refinancing challenges, structural threats, or inflection points in cash flow generation. The strategy maintains a balanced portfolio with a targeted gross exposure of 150% and deploys capital across US and European markets, focusing on companies with a market capitalization above USD 1 billion.

Themis has been live as a stand-alone carve-out since July 2024 and is designed to be a self-sustaining market neutral strategy, aiming for attractive risk-adjusted returns with low correlation to traditional equity markets.

The Themis portfolio typically consists of 30–50 shorts and 20-30 longs positions, with a focus on fundamental differentiation rather than sector or macro bets. Position sizing is carefully calibrated, with gross exposure per position capped at 10% for longs and 5% for shorts. The strategy maintains a risk neutral (Beta) profile, with low net market exposure and minimal beta to broad equity indices. Portfolio construction emphasizes diversification across geographies and industries while maintaining a high conviction in each individual name.

The portfolio is actively managed, with ideas continuously assessed for evolving catalysts, valuation dynamics, and credit/equity signals. Risk is monitored and managed through a combination of proprietary tools, scenario analysis, and firm-level oversight.

General Description. Verition Multi-Strategy Fund LLC and Verition International Multi-Strategy Fund, Ltd. (collectively, the “Fund”) have offered various classes of securities over the years. The net performance returns presented herein were calculated, for certain periods, by adjusting the combined gross profit and loss of the Fund to provide a more direct comparison of the net performance that could have been achieved by the interests currently offered by the Fund (the “Modified Class”).  
In each period, these adjustments reflect: (i) a management fee payable monthly (the “Management Fee”); (ii) an annual incentive allocation/performance fee (subject to a high-water mark) (the “Incentive Allocation”); and (iii) the trading, administrative, operating and Specialty Strategy costs allocated to the Modified Class (“Operating Expenses”).  The Management Fee, Incentive Allocation and Operating Expenses are referred to as the “Modified Class Expenses”.  The rate at which the Management Fee and Incentive Allocation was charged or allocated, as applicable, by the Fund has differed over time.  The Fund has used a consistent Management Fee rate and Incentive Allocation rate to present the pro forma returns for each relevant class, utilizing the current rates for each such class.  The Modified Class Expenses do not include Pass-Through Costs allocated to the Fund’s Initial Class, which are not borne by the Modified Class.  (For a description of “Pass-Through Costs” and the “Initial Class” please refer to the Fund’s offering memoranda.)
March 2008-September 2008. This period presents gross returns of NM Capital LLC (Mr. Maounis’ proprietary account and predecessor to the Fund) (the “Predecessor Account”) adjusted to reflect Modified Class Expenses.  The Predecessor Account was established in January 2008 and only engaged in testing trades prior to March 2008.  Operating Expenses were not borne by the Predecessor Account and Verition does not have specific records showing the actual expenses borne by the Predecessor Account.  The returns reflect an assumed Operating Expenses adjustment based on an assumed expense ratio of 1.43%.  This assumed expense ratio is equal to the actual Operating Expense ratio of the Fund during the period from October 2008-December 2009 and has been included because Verition has determined it represents a reasonable approximation of the Operating Expense ratio that would have been borne by the Predecessor Account during this period given the net asset value of the Predecessor Account and the size of Verition’s operations during this period.  
October 2008-December 2013. This period presents gross returns of the Fund, adjusted on a pro forma basis to reflect Modified Class Expenses.  The Operating Expense adjustment reflects Operating Expenses actually borne by the Fund during this period, including all categories of Operating Expenses currently borne by the Fund.  The Modified Class did not exist during this period, so the Operating Expenses incorporated have been adjusted to remove the impact of Pass-Through Costs allocated to the Initial Class.  
January 2014-April 2020. This period presents gross returns of the Fund, adjusted to reflect Modified Class Expenses.  The Operating Expense adjustment reflects Operating Expenses actually borne by the Funds during this period, which did not include all categories of Operating Expenses currently borne by the Fund.  Had such additional categories of Operating Expenses been borne by the Fund during this period the annualized returns since inception would have been reduced by approximately 0.23% for The Class A Modified Interests/Class C/D Shares, and approximately 0.24% for the Class C Modified Interests and Class G/H Shares.
May 2020-Current. This period presents gross returns of the Fund, adjusted to reflect actual expenses borne by the Modified Interests, including Operating Expenses that are the same as those Operating Expenses currently borne by the Fund.
Specialty Strategies.  Returns prior to November 2014 include the performance of two strategies that were subsequently designated as Specialty Strategies.  Such returns have been reduced to reflect the Operating Expenses associated for these two strategies.  Returns after November 2014 reflect the addition and removal of Specialty Strategies on an ongoing basis and, therefore, represent the historical composite returns of the Modified Classes.  Exposure to Specialty Strategies will incur additional costs and expenses, which are likely to be material.  The classification of Specialty Strategies is reassessed periodically. 
The information contained in this presentation is pro forma and reflects assumptions and calculations that may be incorrect and may be revised at any time without notice. Actual returns to an investor will vary depending on whether they are invested in the Offshore Fund or Onshore Fund, their share class, the timing of their investment and/or any redemption/withdrawal, “new issues” status and other factors. The performance records of each of the Offshore Fund and the Onshore Fund are available upon request. The most recent month’s return is estimated.

results.management_company_description: Founded by Alex Sacerdote in 2006, Whale Rock Capital Management LLC ("Whale Rock") is a Boston-based global long/short equity manager focused on the Technology, Media and Telecom ("TMT") sectors.  Alex and a team of six analysts bring a combined 90+ years of experience in these sectors.  Whale Rock is a growth-oriented manager seeking to benefit from the innovation and disruption inherent in the TMT space. We invest in companies of all capitalization ranges and most subsectors including internet, software, hardware, services and social media. We look across the globe seeking to identify the most attractive opportunities on the long and short side. The firm utilizes a distinctive S-Curve based investment approach.  Our approach is underpinned by intensive and rigorous fundamental research. In a typical year, our team conducts over one thousand face to face meetings with TMT companies in the United States, Asia and Europe. In addition to financial modeling and analysis, the team meets private companies, venture capitalists, customers, competitors and suppliers to gain an in-depth understanding of market dynamics.

results.strategy_description:
The Holocene Children's Fund (the "Children's Fund") is a concentrated, long-only, long term-focused equity fund that launched on February 1, 2022. The Children's Fund is managed by Holocene Advisors, LP ("Holocene"), an investment adviser registered with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission that has managed an equity long/short, beta-neutral fund since 2017 (the "Beta-Neutral Fund"). 

The Children’s Fund seeks to invest in a concentrated, long-only portfolio of companies that we believe have unique business models and whose shares we believe have the potential to compound at high returns over many years. 

The Children's Fund investment program leverages Holocene’s team, infrastructure, collaborative culture, and creative thinking, and the Children's Fund research process is highly integrated and synergistic with the research process that Holocene utilizes in managing the Beta-Neutral Fund. Holocene organizes its sizable investment team by sector/sub-sector coverage, which enables our portfolio managers and analysts to develop deep industry and company knowledge on a global basis. Analysts maintain current research on the companies in their respective coverage universe whether one of Holocene’s strategies is invested at a given time or not. 

As our investment team continually evaluates all companies under our coverage, we come across a small number of companies that do very well in each of the following four areas and are accordingly identified as candidates for inclusion in the Children's Fund portfolio. These four areas are:

(i)	Business Model – the company has a durable, sustainable competitive advantage that we believe will persist and will allow it to earn higher-than-average returns on invested capital over many years; 
(ii)	Capital Allocation and Growth - management is strategic in thinking about capital allocation, and the company should have the ability to grow sustainably at attractive rates and invest its capital at compelling rates of return; 
(iii)	Quality of Management - managers have exceptional skill, motivation, integrity and alignment with shareholders; and 
(iv)	Valuation - we are able to buy the stock at a reasonable price with the potential to generate strong risk-adjusted returns over many years.

In the Children's Fund, we construct a concentrated, long-only, long-term, low-turnover portfolio composed of approximately 20-40 stocks, with the goal of generating strong returns over many years. The Children’s Fund invests predominantly in public mid-cap and large-cap equities on a global basis. We are sector-agnostic in our stock selection given the scarcity of suitable candidates. The Investment Manager generally expects the Children’s Fund to have gross exposure of approximately 100%. 

The Investment Manager also may invest very selectively and opportunistically in private companies. Though we do not hold such investments currently, we offer opt-in and opt-out classes for private investments to accommodate potential investors who do not have the ability to invest in private companies.

The Children's Fund is a limited partnership organized in Delaware, U.S.A., and is available to U.S. taxable, U.S. tax-exempt and non-U.S. investors.

results.strategy_description:
The Holocene Advisors Funds (the "HAF") employ a fundamental, global, equity long/short beta-neutral investment strategy that launched in April 2017. The HAF is managed by Holocene Advisors, LP (the "IM"), an investment adviser registered with the SEC. The IM focuses on alpha generation through disciplined stock selection based on fundamental research conducted by sector-focused investment teams, coupled with analytical, risk-focused portfolio construction to isolate alpha and minimize systematic risk. The Master Fund ("MF") seeks to invest in publicly-traded equities and equity-related instruments across all market capitalizations, though predominantly in U.S.-listed mid and large cap companies.

The IM's sector-focused approach to investing is a defining trait of its investment process. The IM believes that sector specialization is critical to the early identification of investment ideas and can lead to recognition of important nuances, enhance analysts' views on company and industry expectations and timing, and drive idea generation velocity within the Firm.

The IM's investment team is designed to capitalize on its sector-specific research skills while managing risk through portfolio construction. The portfolio of the MF is a single book composed of multiple portfolios of investments as follows:

(1) the "Holocene Book" over which Brandon Haley, Holocene's CIO has full discretion, though certain senior investment team members ("Holocene Book PMs") have a limited ability to make investment decisions on the portions of the portfolio on which they focus; 

(2)(a) dedicated sector-specific portfolios over which certain senior investment team members (each, a "Sector Head") exercise discretion and risk management responsibilities (each, a "Sector Portfolio") and (b) a number of smaller, dedicated sub-sector portfolios over which a select group of analysts (each, an "Epoch PM") exercise discretion and risk management responsibilities (each, an "Epoch Portfolio"); and 

(3) a Capital Markets Portfolio. 

Each portfolio is subject to the oversight of Holocene's CIO and Chief Risk Officer. Sectors covered generally include Consumer, TMT, Industrials, Energy, Healthcare and Financials. The IM's team structure, process and culture encourages collaboration and debate across and within the Holocene Book and Sector Portfolio teams.

The IM strives to maintain strict adherence to a process-oriented, repeatable research process. The goal is to conduct deep, differentiated fundamental research and generate alpha through disciplined stock selection. The IM conducts several stages of due diligence on investment ideas and industry trends including:

Sector-Specific Coverage Model: Each team maintains detailed company-specific models and forecasts on the majority of companies in its sector universe regardless of whether or not the MF is presently active in a name. 

Generation and Refinement of Investment Ideas: Once an idea is identified, the IM initiates a research process that typically includes formal and informal team discussion and debate, exploring cross-sector implications and consequences, seeking to identify potential trends impacting companies and sectors, and unearthing the best way to express the idea (including timing) and the implications for other companies in the sector. 

Due Diligence and Financial Modeling: Thorough research and development of financial models for each company, including, but not limited to, expected value analysis and scenario analysis, various forms of company valuation, and stock multiple upside and downside cases, will be utilized to identify risks and opportunities. 

Position Sizing and Monitoring: Position sizing is a function of the expected return-to-risk ratio of and level of conviction in an investment, and the expected return-to-risk characteristics of the overall portfolio. The investment team generally will analyze 'expected value', portfolio risk, liquidity and short interest, among other considerations, as part of the position sizing process. The IM imposes position size limits across each portfolio and at the MF level. Once a position is initiated, the IM employs a rigorous monitoring process that includes tracking fundamental metrics to monitor the thesis. 

Risk Management: The IM utilizes its internally developed proprietary risk management system. Much of the data that drives risk measurement is built on risk models created by companies such as Barra, while other applications are developed within the IM. Risk management is further served by establishing limits on various sources of risk, thereby allowing for a robust process-driven approach to portfolio construction.
